question: Can I reach you at 2am?
html:
This assistant doesn't have our live-answering hours, so it can't promise that a person will pick up at 2am. If you have an urgent problem, call your local office. The notes below explain what we know about late-night calls.

What we can confirm

  • We run One Hour Heating & Air, Ben Franklin Plumbing and Mister Sparky territories: 19 in Pennsylvania and 6 in New Jersey (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Our overnight staffing, on-call rotation and callback times are not in the data this assistant uses. We won't guess them.
  • Our own planning model assumes about 35% of after-hours calls go unanswered (est.). That is a planning assumption, not a measured rate (Voice AI research).

When late calls come in

Late-night calls are a small share of calls, but a steady one. They rise in summer and are lower in October.

Off-hours call pattern (ServiceTitan data)SummerOctober 2025
All off-hours inbound share, HVAC14.1% (June)9.8%
Weekday after-hours share9.3%6.8%
Weekend share4.9% (August)2.95%
  • Off-hours calls peak between 5 and 9 pm local time, not overnight (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • October is the busiest HVAC month nationally because people start their heating (Punctual Pros demand model).

If you call at 2am

  • Call the number for your local brand.
  • If no one answers, call back or leave a message with your address and the problem.
  • We don't have published callback times, so check again in the morning if you haven't heard from us.

Every 2am call we miss is a homeowner who calls the next company on Google. Our model puts the after-hours share of recoverable jobs at about $390,000 a year (est.), out of about $1.4M (est.) lost to unanswered calls overall (Voice AI research).

Next actions for the operating team

  • Load real hours into this assistant. Confirm overnight coverage by brand and site, then add it so this answer can give a firm yes or no.
  • Measure the missed-call rate. Pull ServiceTitan or CRM call logs to replace the 35% after-hours assumption and the 14.8% blended missed-call share (est.) with measured rates.
  • Pilot AI overflow answering overnight. Vendor figures show 70% booking overall and 90% when capacity is open. These numbers are self-reported and unaudited, so treat them as ranges. Run a short pilot to get our own figures.
  • Staff for heating season now. It is Oct 8, 2026, and October is the busiest HVAC month (Punctual Pros demand model). Check the on-call rotation before cold snaps arrive.
